C5.defect: Introduction and N2 strengthen if to only if; some long anchors lose the predicate.
C5.cards: Distinguish A if B (B implies A) from A only if B (A implies B). The fact that a text proves growth under an instrumental definition does not rule out growth under other definitions. Audit necessity words in every prose sentence and table cell, including summaries and exceptions; never insert only, must or requires without an anchored necessity predicate. Give an explicit source only-if condition its own relation when it is central to a counterexample. Use separate contiguous spans shorter than 180 characters when a full conditional would be clipped.
C5.brief: Before delivery, compare every if/only-if/under condition in the introduction and both tables with the source direction. A stipulated sufficient condition must not silently become necessary. Keep possibility and speaker attribution. Avoid long clipped quotations: use two short predicate-bearing spans and preserve the entire needed conditional across them.

I4.defect: Malformed critic rows leave all nine findings without valid rulings; anchor locality and unsupported policy assessments.
I4.cards: Choose short spans naming the actor and action, plus the consequence or qualifier in a second span. Do not use This resulted or Nothing guarantees without an anchor identifying the antecedent. Separate an operational aim from an excluded-cost claim if two spans cannot carry both. Qualitative feasibility and effectiveness are unknown when the source supplies no specified proposal and no assessment of its implementability; an earlier arrangement does not establish the feasibility of unspecified moderate policies.
I4.brief: Keep documented conflict-induced responses distinct from consensual cooperation and proposed remedies. Use unknown for the feasibility/effectiveness of an unspecified proposal. Use short actor-and-predicate spans that can be checked without rewriting multiple claims in one ledger row. Preserve the prescribed ledger grammar: one finding per row and, when revising, exactly one revised-finding field, with separate anchor and anchor-b fields rather than a nested example ledger.

E3.defect: Final body and table citations point to wrong meanings after ledger renumbering.
E3.cards: Keep each finding ID tied to one stable claim. When quoting a final ID in a table, read that final row and confirm that it actually expresses the claim in the cell; existence of the ID is insufficient. Preserve separate observations for procurement, alternative-project development, private finance, selective engagement and ownership. General background or a nearby similarly numbered row cannot substitute for the specific observation.
E3.brief: Set the final ledger identities before writing the reading and tables; preserve those identities throughout delivery. Do not remove a row and shift later IDs after the table has been written. For every citation in the actual final prose and each table cell, reread its final ledger row for actor, action, scope and qualifier. Correct the citation or remove the claim if it refers to a different observation. Duplicate paraphrases do not repair a missing relation. Retain the distinction between shared fit and discrimination; source-reported and analyst-derived predictions stay marked.

I11.defect: PEACE/EMA combined table gives both projects the EMA after-exclusion chronology.
I11.cards: Preserve each project or asset identity through every grouped relation. A source stating that project B followed an exclusion does not date project A or make A a response merely because both are parallel alternatives. Distinguish operational status, proposed routing, reported response and purchase intention. Use separate rows when a shared heading would transfer chronology or causality. Select short spans containing the operational/action predicate rather than the opening project name.
I11.brief: Audit every combined-project row for transferred dates, causes or completion status. Keep a pre-existing operational cable separate from a later reported response project even when both bypass an exclusion. No combined PEACE/EMA after-exclusion origin is licensed by a source that attributes the response only to EMA. Use short separate spans for operation, ownership, route and response; map table claims to the final specific findings rather than a generic component label.

T5.defect: Repeated anchor fields invalidate the critic ledger; all 22 rows retained without rulings.
T5.cards: Use one source-supported directional claim per row, with short separate spans that name both the starting object and the change predicate. Replace anaphoric openings with a second antecedent span when needed. Every anchor field must have a unique suffix: one anchor, one anchor-b, one anchor-c if necessary; never repeat anchor or embed a revised ledger inside an anchor field. Preserve conditional successful communication rather than guaranteeing that every new application diffuses.
T5.brief: Build the dynamic inventory from predicate-bearing evidence packets with each quoted span under 180 characters where possible. Keep the source-described cycle separate from a formally signed feedback loop, and label any missing or conditional return. Do not carry a compound claim under a nearby different ID. Follow the prescribed critic ledger grammar without repeated anchor/revised-finding fields; revise the one row in place using distinct anchor suffixes.

R2.defect: Sonnet 7.667 below original 8.500; checked reading loses useful argumentative moves and source qualifications.
R2.cards: Recover the source-specific persuasive operations that a simplified appeals map can miss: distinguish a definitional identity claim from an appeal to what an author would have conceded; test the cumulative force of separately named objections rather than treating their count as proof. Read consequential notes and qualifying passages as part of the argument. Preserve changes in the target theory over time and concessions of limited usefulness. A useful borrowing from an author is not automatically a contradiction of rejecting that authors distinctive theory.
R2.brief: Give a full text-specific rhetorical reading, preserving the best questions of the original. In Harris, inspect the refusal-to-concede inference, the eight objections and their dependencies, the occupational and colonial examples, and the qualifications in notes 2 and 5 about changing Honneth and labour. Distinguish the source allowing recognition as a component of a different theory from the claim that its monism cannot be repaired; do not inflate selective agreement into contradiction. Carry a consequential counter-passage through the argument and tables. Avoid invented effects or hidden motives, and keep scope/coverage claims confined to the actual retained findings.

I9.defect: Sonnet 8.167 below original 8.500; broader source distinctions were lost despite improved anchoring.
I9.cards: Retain the source distinctions that carry the boundary critique: means versus ends, separate firm attribution versus collective production, given preferences versus socially produced wants, the model treating the economy as separable from social history, provisional national abstraction versus heterogeneous global production, and approximate temporal phases. Identify who draws each boundary and whether it is a criticized exclusion or an explicitly provisional analytical device. Do not infer a hidden agenda from the existence of a beneficiary.
I9.brief: Make the boundary reading as useful and specific as the best original questions: trace manufactured preferences, regulation versus mobile capital, and periodization where the source supplies them, alongside firm accounting and excluded harms. Test the critique against the author's acceptance of approximate regularities, provisional national abstraction and effective production; do not mistake a qualified working model for a claim of universal separability. Include only source-supported burdens/bearers and label proposed reframings. Keep complete/partial coverage distinct from semantic approval, use exact scope field names, and do not claim broader findings than the final ledger retains.
